utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know whether he was. He sometimes drove me. He was a driver in the brigade, not in the corps, and sometimes he would drive me. And at that particular occasion, I don't know if it was me and my son -- it is possible that that person, the driver went with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What about Stevan Stevanovic? Did he go with you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, not on that occasion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What about Mile Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Mile Kosoric was the brigade commander. How would you expect him to come with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. What route did you take?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Vlasenica, Milici, Konjevic Polje, Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what time did you reach Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It took us slightly less than an hour to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims on the way? Any Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, there was only a police patrol in Konjevic Polje. It was already late in the afternoon. There was a police patrol in Konjevic Polje, and then there was another one in Kravica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see the MUP police stationed along the road, the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac Road, every hundred, metres or so?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't notice any such thing. I remember having seen a patrol. I remember that a hundred per cent, and I also remember the other one in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So we've heard evidence in this case that before the fish dinner, there was a meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters that was attended by General Mladic, General Krstic, Vinko Pandurevic, Radomir Furtula, Milenko Jevdzevic, Mirko Trivic, and others. What do you know about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, we brought the dinner. There were some soldiers on duty there. I reported to them, and I said to them, I brought dinner. Where am I to serve it, in which room? Then we went to that room. We left. Before we did that, we laid the table. Then I wanted to return, but then I was asked to wait for some five or ten minutes more, and some officers appeared after they had ended the meeting. I greeted Mladic. He thanked me for having brought the dinner. I also said hello to Krstic, and then I went home. I had guests in my own house. I couldn't stay any longer. I was rushed to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Was the dinner in a different room from the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: In a different room, yes. We laid a table, and we served dinner in a different room. I don't know whether they actually had the dinner where we left it or whether they took the food somewhere else after we left. I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So was the fish on the table when they came into the dinner, or did you go into the meeting room with the fish?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: We served the fish on oval plates in that room, and we left some wine and some brandy there, and I met with all of them in the corridor after I had laid the food on the table in that room. I greeted them, and then I left. I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So you didn't walk into the meeting with the fish?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've had a lot of time to think about this dinner. Can you tell us who was there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know who actually attended dinner. I only saw them in the corridor as they were leaving the meeting room, and I told you that I said hello to Mladic and Krstic. I also saw Jevdjevic, and I saw Vinko as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What about Mirko Trivic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I didn't -- no, I don't remember who else was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. No, I didn't, no. What do you mean? What are we talking about? You said that I mentioned him that evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: No, sir. You said you saw these officers come out of the meeting room and you saw them in the corridor, and I'm trying to get you to tell us which officers you saw in the corridor. Did you see General Zivanovic in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I notice Mr. Sarapa standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did not say the officers leaving the meeting room. He said that he saw them in the corridor once they had all come from the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But I think -- let's proceed anyway. I'm happy with what we had in the transcript in any case. Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So besides General Mladic, General Krstic, Milenko Jevdjevic, and Vinko Pandurevic, you don't recall who else was there, who else you saw in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, you said that you left Bratunac that night and went back home; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see the buses and trucks in Bratunac that night?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I did not. It was already dark. It was night, and before the gate of the command did not see anything. The command is at the entrance to Bratunac. I never entered the town itself. And the command building is actually on the main road. You turn left, and you leave Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What about the next day? What did you do the day after the dinner?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Around 8.00 the following day, I went to church. The liturgy started at 9.00. I went there early to prepare everything in the church, to have a word with the priest and discuss the protocol because the Episcope Vasilije was coming, and on that day the liturgy is a festive one different to the one served by a common priest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What time was the dinner that you --

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I did not finish my answer. You asked me about the whole day, and I only told you about the morning, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Shall I continue, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: And the service in church lasted until about one hour because after the liturgy we had a procession through the town. Church icons and standards are brought out of the church, and everybody who attended the mass in the church walk behind the icons and standards. They walked in a circle in one part of the town, and then we returned to the church. Then the celebration cake or the festive cake is broken in the church, and after that we went to have lunch in the hotel, and General Zivanovic also attended that lunch in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What time was that lunch?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What time was that lunch?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I remember that the church service ended around 1.00, and after 1.00 we went to the hotel, and we stayed there until midnight. We were sitting in the hotel socialising. We were singing. The atmosphere was very festive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see buses go through the middle of Vlasenica that day, buses full of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, not in the morning. My house is on the road, and I didn't see anybody passing by it. The church is in the very centre of the town. I didn't see anything there, and then we went to the hotel, and there was nothing going on around the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. What about the following day? What did you do that day? Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: On the following day, it was a -- everybody was hung over. Some people had breakfast, those who overnighted at the hotel, and then we continued socialising until noon. I believe that it lasted until noon, but we were pretty much hung over from all the brandy that we had the previous day. We saw our guests off, we tidied up the hotel, and then the waiters and the cooks who had served us the day before joined us the following day for a bit of socialising, and then they shared the leftovers with us. It's a good thing to do. You are not supposed to throw leftovers. It's better to eat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere that day? Did you leave Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. Either on that day or on the following day I went to Srebrenica, but I can't remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what was your purpose in going to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: My best man and I went there, out of curiosity. We wanted to see what Srebrenica looked like from inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: The town was deserted. It was empty. It looked ghastly. All the buildings were covered with smoke, and there were logs and woods on the roads, and there were some elderly people roaming around the town. There were some soldiers as well. That's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I passed through Potocari, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: There were people in Potocari. On both sides of the road were soldiers and police and UNPROFOR soldiers and people. Yes, I did pass through there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see any VRS officers there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No. I did not stay any time there. I just passed through.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you see Muslims there? Is that the people you were describing on either side of the road?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Muslims in Potocari, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Were there buses there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And what was happening? Were the Muslims being put on the buses?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: As we were passing through, I could see people getting on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Could you see the men being separated from their families before they were getting on the buses?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No. We slowed down. We moved slowly. We passed by and we looked. I did look at the people, but I did not see anyone being separated. I did not see it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You said you went there with your best man. Can you give us his name?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Stevan Stevanovic. You mentioned him just a minute ago as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You took the same car that you took to Bratunac, the Golf?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. What about the day after you went to Srebrenica? Did you go anywhere that day?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't go anywhere. I stayed in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You didn't go to Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I did go, but I don't know whether it was on that day or the day after. I know that I went to Pale for a day, but I don't know which day it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What did you go there for?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I went to see President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: For what purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Because on the following day they took all the people somewhere.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed a word, but I believe that it was Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That people were taken to Kladanj, and that's what I asked President Karadzic about. I asked him who those people were and where they were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mentioned a place. Did you mention Kladanj? Was it Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, people were driven in the direction of Kladanj. That's what I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Which people?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: What? What are you referring to? What people?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, you said people were driven in the direction of Kladanj. I'm asking you which people are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, Muslims in the buses, the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The Muslim population from where?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Probably from Potocari or Srebrenica. Those people, they were all brought and taken from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So you went to ask President Karadzic about these people, the Muslims being taken from Srebrenica to Kladanj. What did he say?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was fuming with rage. He was very angry. He was in no mood to talk about anything. He told me, Puska, go home, mind your own business. I never saw him so angry. Never before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is that all he said?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: What was he angry about?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: How should I know? He was angry. I've never seen him so angry before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And how long did this meeting last for?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: A minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can you recall what time of day it was?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: In the evening or late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please go to 65 ter 4409. May I have a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document dated the 20th of November, 1992. You can read it there: "Upon evident necessity and in order to ensure preconditions for the implementation of official tasks for the needs of Military Post 7111 Han Pijesak, I order to hand over to Zvonko Bajagic passenger vehicle VW Golf, registration number P7105." Is that your car, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: That was the car I had originally, and it was stolen from me in Sabac; that's in Serbia. And then I used my car to drive around, but its registration plates were changed into military registration plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please look at 65 ter 4418.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is a vehicle log for VW Golf with the registration plates P7105 for July 1995, and you are the first name on there; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, I have the original here. This might be easier for you to look at. Now, according to this vehicle log, it was refueled with 45 litres of fuel on the 12th of July. Did you refuel this car with 45 litres of fuel on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It wasn't me. I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Is that your signature on the line that says 12 July?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't. No, none of the signatures is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at a couple of other documents that might help refresh your recollection. Can we go to 65 ter 4419. Mr. President, it's break time. We might be able to do this after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much longer do you reckon you'll be putting questions, Mr. Mitchell?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's taken longer than I expected, Your Honour. It could be -- I will finish today, but it could be most of the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell. Let's try to conclude, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, we were talking about the refueling of your car with 45 litres of fuel on the 12th of July, and you said that it wasn't you. So I'd like to show you a couple of documents to help refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to 65 ter 4419.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is an authorisation to refuel a vehicle with the registration plates P7105 with 45 litres of fuel. It's authorising to you refuel that car. It's dated the 13th of July. Can you tell us why the vehicle log would say 12 July but the authorisation says 13 July?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, you saw earlier that I did not receive it, didn't sign for it, and I have no idea. I see my name is written here, but where did I sign? You must have my signature somewhere so you can compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: How would I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Can we please look at 65 ter 4420.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This is the Drina Corps fuel distribution list from 10 to 13 July. You can see the very last entry on the page, 45 litres of fuel; that same vehicle, P7105; Zvonko Bajagic; and your signature underneath.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: This is not my signature. Somebody forged this. It's obvious that it's not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go back to 65 ter 4418, the vehicle log. If we can go to page 2 in both the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Now, sir, that's a trip. If we look at the entry on the 13th of July: Vlasenica, Srebrenica, Vlasenica. That's your trip to Srebrenica that you told us about; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I see there must be some confusion here. This is a military vehicle. I saw there in the order the name Mile Kosoric, commander of the brigade, and Sekulic and I; and I told you earlier I also had my own private car, and I never poured military fuel in my private car. That's the confusion. Out of the three persons mentioned there, one must have tanked up in my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, we saw your name on the front of this vehicle log. Is that or is that not your trip to Srebrenica on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I went in my own car. I told you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is not the car you went in; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did not go in that vehicle, and I did not take any fuel. I did not take petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So it's just a mistake that this vehicle log lists a trip to Srebrenica on the day you said you went there and you signed -- there's a fuel authorisation for 45 litres in your name. You don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Let us see who signed that. Let's compare my signature and the signature on that paper. It's not mine, and you can see all the people who are authorised to use this vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So we can see there's also a trip on the 14th of July: Vlasenica, Pal, Vlasenica, Loko. Now, you told us that you went to see President Karadzic around this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you take this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: On that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So you took it on the 14th, but you didn't take it on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, you might want to have a look at the original here. The handwriting on the 13th and 14th is almost identical.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can see that, but I did not fill in any orders or logs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mitchell, can you ask the witness to read the route again for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: On the 14th, Judge Kwon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, can you please have a look at the vehicle log and read out the route --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or we may zoom up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see that. Do you want me to write it all down the way it's written here and then you can compare?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read the route which is written on the date of 14th July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vlasenica, Pal, Vlasenica, Loko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you say Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pal. It's actually written P-a-l, like, short for Pale, or it could be Vlasenica Loko, Vlasenica Loko, one of the two. No, no, this is not Pale either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My attention has been drawn that Mr. Pandurevic would like to consult his counsel. Yes, so Mr. Sarapa, I suppose you are the only one who can approach him. Mr. Sarapa, I understand that your client wishes to have a word with his Defence team. Since you speak the language, I suggest that you either approach him or you go somewhere and see what he needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can talk here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you need to consult with Mr. Haynes, Mr. Sarapa, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not now. All right. Okay. Thank you. It may be too late afterwards. Let's continue. Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we please go to 65 ter 3876, page 41 in the English and page 91 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is Radovan Karadzic's appointment diary for 1995, which was obtained when he was arrested last year. On 14 July, we can see two entries with your name. The first is call Zvonko Bajagic, and the second is a meeting between you and President Karadzic between 12.35 a.m. on the morning of the 15th and 1.25 a.m. Earlier, you told us that you met with the president for about a minute. That's a 50-minute meeting, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Which day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The last entry on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sorry, we need to scroll down. The last entry on that page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, my question was, earlier today you testified that when you met with President Karadzic he was very angry, and you stayed there for about a minute.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: That was the evening of the 13th, and this is the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, you told us, you testified under oath that you went to Pale the following day after the day that you went to Srebrenica. You went so Srebrenica on the 13th; you went to Pale on the 14th. This is what President Karadzic's appointment diary says on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: When you asked me the next day, I thought the next day after the patron saints day, which would be the 13th, and this is the 14th, because my sighting of those buses taking people somewhere was on the 13th, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, when we were talking about the 13th, I asked you did you see any buses, and you told me that your house was on the main road and that you -- you didn't see any buses.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any on the 12th. On the patron saint's day, I didn't see any. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, did you meet with President Karadzic at any other point in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I think I was there that night, as you see written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Did you meet with him on any additional occasions apart from this meeting that we can see on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. Maybe, if you remind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 38 in the English, page 85 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: On the 3rd of July, we can see at 1400 hours Zvonko Bajagic, he left, and there's little minus sign at the start of that, at the start of that entry. So that means that you went to Pale but you didn't actually get to meet with the president; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to page 44 in the English, page 100 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And we're looking at the entry under 31 July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have to scroll it down, I think. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Zvonko Bajagic meeting with President Karadzic for two and a half hours. Do you recall what that meeting was about?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, really. On the 31st, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Well, that's just after the Muslim population has been bussed out of the Zepa enclave. Did you talk to him about that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No. On the 31st, no. I don't know anything about Zepa, when people were taken away or anything. I don't know where they were taken either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: But you can't recall what you spoke with him about for two and a half hours?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go back to 65 ter 4418. It's page 2 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S. If we can blow that up again, those trips on the 13th and the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, you'll agree with me that there's no trip recorded in this vehicle log for the 11th of July, 1995, is there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: There's no trip recorded in this vehicle log for the 11th of July, is there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can see there's no record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to suggest to you that you did fill out this car with 45 litres of fuel on the night of 12th July, as the front of the vehicle log indicates, right before you left for this dinner in Bratunac; and on 13 July you went to Srebrenica, returned to Vlasenica where the vehicle log and the fuel authorisations were filled out; then on 14 July, you went to Pale, and you met with President Karadzic for 50 minutes as we saw in his appointment diary. So isn't this really what happened on the 12th, 13th, and 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Could you break that question into three short ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, I think we've been through this in a lot of detail over the last couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: What did you mean to ask me a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, I'm suggesting to you that you did fill up this car on the night of 12 July on your way to this dinner at Bratunac. The next day, you go to Srebrenica; then you return to Vlasenica where those fuel documents were filled out. Then I'm suggesting that on the 14th of July, you took this vehicle to Pale and you met with the president, and we saw --

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Slowly. Let's take things at a time. Now you are saying that I brought that dinner on the 12th? Give me a document to say that I signed, and I will tell you that I didn't. I gave you my answer already. The dinner was on the 11th. You are mixing things. That car could have been driven by anybody, whoever came to take it. You can see that there are three names on the travel log for that day. You can see the names of the people who were allowed to drive the car. I'm offering to show you how I sign my name. I'm offering to show you my signature so you can compare what you see before you and my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, the authorisations for 45 litres of fuel were made out in your name; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I've seen that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, it's the Prosecution's position that we've proven beyond a reasonable doubt that this meeting and the dinner at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters happened on the evening of the 12th of July, and that you are not telling the truth as you sit here today.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: You say what you want. How could it have been on the 12th? On the 12th was the day when you were supposed to eat meat. This would be like not eating meat on Christmas or asking me if I eat meat at Christmas or not, if I eat fish at Christmas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, let me confirm something you said earlier. You told us about a big celebration at Vlasenica where there was over a thousand people there.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I didn't not say a thousand. No, sir. I said that there were about 200 guests at the dinner. There were about 200 people on the day. On the eve of St. Peter's Day, there were about 40 people; and on St. Peter's Day, there were about 200 invited guests.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. And this big party, this big gathering in Vlasenica was the day after you took the fish to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Are you understanding me when I say the 11th and -- when I say the 11th? The 11th is on the eve of the St. Peter's Day, the day of fasting, which ends at midnight. The 12th, St. Peter's Day, we no longer fasted on that day. We had this big lunch to celebrate the day, on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking, sir. This big lunch was the day after the dinner at the Bratunac Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 4434 in e-court. I apologise, we don't have a translation of this in e-court yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: But, sir, can you take a look at this document and tell us what it is? Sir, I'm told that what this document says is the assistance is being issued for preparation of celebration of patron saint's day at the Vlasenica SO and the Vlasenica SDS to Zvonko Bajagic, the host from Vlasenica, who is the host of the celebration. The president and vice-president of the RS are going to attend the celebration. The items should be registered and discharged as assistance.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: And what date was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That was just what I was going to ask you, sir. Can we scroll back up. They are talking about preparations for this on the 13th of July, aren't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: 13 July? That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So this is a mistake?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: A mistake. Take the church call calendar and see when St. Peter's Day is, when it is celebrated. And let me just explain one more thing: This may have been taken for the celebration as starters, but the paper may have still been issued on the 13th. And look here, why would we need fruit marmelade or liver pate? Why would we need tinned food? We had pork, lamb, cake, stews, cooked food. Why would we need any of the tinned food? Why would we need bacon? What would that be for? And can you scroll down a little. It says that president and vice-president would attend. That's what you read out, isn't that? President and vice-president are to attend the celebration. This is also a mistake. They were not there, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Sir. I want to ask you one last question. Do you know Lieutenant-Colonel --

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm begging your pardon. And this, again, is not my signatures where it says issued to personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not saying that that is your signature. Who is Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubo Sobot.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubo Sobot was the assistant commander for logistics in the brigade in Sekovici when the brigade was first established. And later, he was transferred to the Drina Corps, but I don't know when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Can we look at, just briefly, 65 ter 4419.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that you had no idea whose signature this is.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's Lieutenant-Colonel Sabot's signature, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. So why didn't he sign Sobot? Why would he sign my name? And excuse me, what document is that? The document for the fuel, is that what we're talking about, the fuel document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's an authorisation for to you fill up your car with 45 litres of fuel signed by the officer in charge, Ljubo Sobot; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I can see that this was in my name, and it was signed by Ljubo Sobot, but I never took that fuel. It could have been anybody else, and it did happen occasionally. I can only tell you that. And the same is true of the foodstuff. Somebody took all that food on my behalf, the potatoes and the pates; that's just crazy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bajagic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there re-examination, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, you've described your house, your collection. Could you please tell us, did you acquire all that during the war, or did you have all the things even before the war?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Everything that I had and I still have, and I had three times more stuff before the war broke out. I acquired all that before the war, and during the war up to the present day, I've had to sell things to survive because my family has ten members and nobody is employed. The only person who has been in gainful employment for five months is my daughter-in-law. And the things that I have are all my inheritance, and the ethnological collection that I have around my house is something that I've been collecting for years, and I still have retained some very unique artifacts and examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You were shown several intercepts. Jovo Kundacina is a name mentioned in one of these conversations. Do you know a person by that name?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I saw that, and I said that this was not my dialect, that I did not and I do not speak like that. I know Jovo Kundacina just a little. I know that he was an assistant for logistics somewhere, I believe it was in Bijeljina, but I don't know whose logistics it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: In answering the Prosecutor's question -- questions about mobilisation in 1991, you spoke about how it was done. Was there a command of the Yugoslav People's Army in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander was Milosevic, who was either colonel or lieutenant-colonel at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, on the 11th of July when you went to Bratunac to take the dinner there, you said that you took your own car there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes. The work log that you were shown depicting the dates, the 13th, the 14th and other dates, that work log indicates that four different drivers used that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: You could see if for yourself. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show P4418, page 2 in Serbian, page 3 in English, please. Could we please blow up the Serbian version of this text a little bit more, if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, could you please look at the date 1407 -- or the time 1407. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: In the middle it says "Vlasen" and then -- "Vlasen" in the Cyrillic script; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: The first letter of the middle word, could it also be a letter M?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And what about the second letter of that word? Is it an A, or could it be an I?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It could also be a T because it has a cross across the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: However, is it a Cyrillic A, or is it a Cyrillic I?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Well, it could also be a J and an A and I. How should I know? It could be anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Let me ask you this.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It is the Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes, it is the Cyrillic. In the Cyrillic script, could this also be read as "Mil"?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, it could also be read as "Mil."

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: What would it mean when it says "Vlasen"; shortened for "Vlasenica," isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And then "Vlasen," again, a shortened version of Vlasenica, and then in the middle, "Mil." What would "Mil" stand for?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It could stand for Vlasenica Milici Vlasenica. That sounds plausible enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And now I would ask you about the 13th of July, which is immediately above the 14th, above what we have just read out. It says here, as you can see, "Vlasen," which is abbreviated Vlasenica, then which "Srebre," which means Srebrenica, and then Vlasenica, and there's no doubt about that. How many kilometres were travelled on the 13th of July between Vlasenica, Srebrenica, Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: There's something else. It says Vlasenica, Srebrenica, and something else in small letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: It is Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: On the 13th, Vlasen is Vlasenica, is it not? There's no doubt about that. Then Srebre, that would be abbreviated Srebrenica, and then after that we have Vlase, standing for Vlasenica. After that, in that same line where the mileage is indicated, is there anything there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: No, there's nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: What does it mean to you, the mileage is not recorded? What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Maybe that's what was planned, but nobody went -- nobody travelled that route on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Which car did you take to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: My own Golf. I've already told you at least ten times so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Very well. In this travel log on the 15th, it says -- for the 15th of July. Could you please concentrate on that. It says Vlasenica, Milici, Pale, Vlasenica. Does this mean or confirm that on the 15th you went to Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Look here. It says 130 kilometres there, and you say Vlasenica Milici. And this is only 15 kilometres, and Milici, whether it says Pale here or not, from Milici to Pale there is 110 kilometres. From Pale back to Vlasenica is, again, 90 kilometres plus local journeys. It should all in all be at least 250 kilometres in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now produce P4402 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: 4420, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, 4420. [Interpretation] Could we please scroll up to see all the entries for the 13th of July, and I'm talking about the Serbian text, please. 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, you see the entries for the 13th of July, starting with number 35, that's the first entry, and on this page it ends with number 41. Can you see all that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: 13 July 1995, there is figure 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And now you have number 41 where it says 45. That's the number next to it.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: 45, you can see that. Well, do you see and can you tell us when this could have been written and signed? We are looking at the last column after the numbers. Do you see the names? I'm sure you see the names from 35 to 41, and signatures. When should this have been signed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: From 35 to 41?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: What are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: When should all these have been signed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean? What should have been signed?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Look at the signatures in the last column. Signatures in the last column, you can see different names, different family names, different signatures belonging to the people.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Was that entered on the same day?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: On the same day?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: How should I know? I did not make the entries, did I? I can see different names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: It says Bajagic Zvonko here.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO BAJAGIC
utterances.text: It's not my signature. People, how can you not understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any further questions, Mr. Sarapa, because our time is up already by five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to ask him a question. Sorry to the next Chamber. Can I see page P4418 again, whether it is Pale or Milici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Judge Kwon, we have the original here if you'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, show him, too, the original, please. Let's take a look at the 14th. You remember that entry, Mr. Bajagic? When Mr. Mitchell from the Prosecution asked about that entry to you, you answered this way. It's at page 57, line 21, so I shall read it again, Mr. Bajagic: "We can see there's also a trip on the 14th of July, Vlasenica, Pal, Vlasenica, Loko. You told us that you went to see President Karadzic around this time; correct? "Yes. "Did you take this vehicle on that day? "... yes." Do you stand by what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the gentleman has totally confused me when he trapped me into looking at these travel logs. If I were to swear, I couldn't tell you whether I took the military car or my own, but it says here Vlasenica, Pale, Vlasenica. Vlasenica, Pale, and back to Vlasenica, only that is 180 kilometres. That journey alone is 180 kilometres because Vlasenica to Pale is 90 kilometres in one direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bajagic, on behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over to give evidence, and I wish you a safe journey back home. We'll come to documents, this and the previous witness tomorrow. Thank you. Registrar, if you could kindly communicate to the next Chamber our apologies and explain that we overstayed in order to finish the testimony of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 10th day of March, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
